description: Machine-readable REST + realtime endpoint inventory for the Mineral Bridge backend. Paths are relative to each client basePrefix; fullPath is the mounted Express path. Parsed programmatically from the three API-ENDPOINTS.md files; counts verified against the declared totals.

conventions.auth: Bearer access token (15 min) + refreshToken in JSON body (60 d, rotating, stored in Keychain/Keystore). No passwords; phone + 6-digit SMS OTP. Optional X-Transaction-Pin header on bids, withdrawals, account delete.

conventions.pagination: cursor: ?limit&cursor -> { data: [], meta: { limit, nextCursor, total?, counts? } }; single resources are bare

realtime.note: Realtime channel is also REST endpoint #60 (GET), so it is included in restCount (139) and NOT additive. Heartbeat 15 s; Last-Event-ID replay window 10 min.

documentedDiscrepancies: Admin API-ENDPOINTS has no dedicated realtime section: the only push channel is SSE GET /auctions/{auctionId}/bids/stream (#60), already counted in the 139. Other "live" surfaces are polled (chain events 15 s, counters/bell 60 s, rate feed 120 s).

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Request bodies differ. Mobile: { phone (E.164), intent: signup|login, channel?: sms|voice|whatsapp } -> { challengeId, expiresIn: 60, resendAfter: 42, channel, maskedPhone, accountExists } (6-digit SMS). Web: { method: mobile|email|whatsapp, identifier, intent } -> same shape as POST /auth/register response { challengeId, method, target, expiresIn, codeLength: 4 }. Web supports email OTP, mobile does not. Mobile returns accountExists (enumeration risk); web contract forbids revealing account existence. Different rate limits (web: 3/identifier/15 min, 10/IP/h).
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Different request AND response. Mobile: { challengeId, phone, code (6 digits), device{id,platform,name,pushToken} } -> { accessToken, refreshToken (in BODY), expiresIn: 900, isNewAccount, account{ id, fullName, phone, tier, kyc{status:none|...}, onboarding{nextStep} } }. Web: { challengeId, code (4 digits) } -> { accessToken, expiresIn, tokenType, user: UserProfile, kycStatus: unverified|pending|verified, isNewAccount } + Set-Cookie mb_refresh (refresh token NOT in body). Error codes: mobile 422 auth/otp-invalid, 410 auth/otp-expired; web 401 auth/invalid-credentials, 401 auth/otp-expired. Mobile never sets a cookie; web never returns refreshToken in the body. OTP length 6 vs 4 means challenges are NOT interchangeable across clients.
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Mobile: { challengeId } -> 200 same body as /auth/otp/request, 429 auth/otp-rate-limited before resendAfter. Web: listed in API-ENDPOINTS (#4) and error registry only; API-CONTRACT.md has NO schema section for it. Assume { challengeId } -> request response; confirm with web team.
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Mobile: requires X-Transaction-Pin header, no body, 204 on success, 409 auth/account-deletion-blocked { blockingOrders[] }. Web: body { confirmation: "DELETE", reason? }, 202 { scheduledDeletionAt, openOrderCount } (async/scheduled), 409 auth/account-has-open-orders { openOrderCount }. Success status (204 vs 202) and error codes differ. Web users have no transaction PIN.
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Mobile: { data: [{ id, deviceName, platform, current, lastActiveAt, location }], meta:{total} }. Web: { items: [{ id, device, location, lastActiveAt, isCurrent, ipAddress (last octet masked) }] }. Different envelope key (data vs items) and field names (current vs isCurrent, deviceName vs device).
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Both: 204; revoking the current session returns 409 (mobile: unspecified code, "use sign-out"; web: auth/cannot-revoke-current). Align on web code auth/cannot-revoke-current for both.
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Completely different payloads. Mobile: buy-side requirement { productId|cartId, quantity{value,unit g|kg|t}, neededBy, delivery{...importPermitNumber (Tier 3)}, acceptedTerms } -> 201 flat order { id ord_*, reference MB-YYYY-NNNNN, status: verifying, paymentTaken:false, nextSteps[] }; no payment is taken; Idempotency-Key required; 403 kyc/not-verified. Web: purchase request { lotId, quantity{unit g|kg|oz|ct|MT}, paymentMethod: escrow|wire|lc|btc, quoteId?, deliveryAddress?, payoutMethodId?, notes? } -> 201 { order, nextAction{kind,url} }; 403 kyc/not-approved; 409 lot/*; 409 order/quote-expired. Different catalog entity (product vs lot), different KYC error code, different quote flow (mobile POST /orders/requirements/price vs web POST /orders/quote).
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Mobile: ?tab=active|completed&limit&cursor, BUY-side only (selling is GET /sell/requests); returns { data[], meta:{limit,nextCursor,counts:{active,selling,completed}} }; items carry status in_transit|verifying|..., statusLabel, tone, stage{current,total,label}, progress int, eta{from,to,display}, value Money{scale,display}. Web: ?side=buy|sell&status=active|completed&page&perPage; returns { items[], page, perPage, total }; items carry status in_review|active|complete|rejected|cancelled, side BUY|SELL, stage{index,total,title,subtitle}, progressPercent, rejected, closed, lot{...gradientFrom/To}. Different pagination model (cursor vs page), status enums, ID style (ord_* + reference vs "MB-ORDER-33056" as id), and scope (web includes sell orders).
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Mobile: flat order { escrow{funded,amount,...}, assay{finalWeight,purity}, seal, carrier, eta, canConfirmDelivery, version }. Web: { order, settlement{method,status,escrowReference,releasedAt}, counterparty, cancellable }. Non-ASM web orders can be SELL side; mobile orders never are. Web returns 403 (never 404) for non-party callers.
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single route handler; branch on req.client (X-Client) to select request validator and response mapper. Same Mongoose model underneath.

auth.web: wsToken in query string (?token=), issued from GET /auth/me

sharedPathConflicts.notes: Same URL under /v1, different handshake: mobile forbids tokens in the query string and uses the subprotocol header; web requires a dedicated short-lived wsToken in the query string because browsers cannot set WS headers. Event sets differ: mobile bid.placed{bid,highestBid,bidCount,reserveMet,version}, bidder.outbid{auctionId,auctionName,newHighestBid,closesAt,yourBid}, auction.extended{reason: "anti_sniping"}, auction.closed{outcome: won|lost|reserve_not_met,winningBid,yourBid}; web bid.placed{bidId,amount,bidderLabel,placedAt,bidCount,minimumNextBid}, bidder.outbid{yourBid,currentBid,auctionName}, auction.extended{closesAt,reason: "anti_snipe"}, auction.closing{secondsRemaining}, auction.closed{finalBid,outcome: won|lost|unsold,settlementOrderId}. Envelope differs: mobile { event, at, data }; web { event, sequence, sentAt, data }.
sharedPathConflicts.resolution: Single upgrade handler; accept either handshake, resolve client from the credential type / X-Client, and emit client-specific frames.

semanticOverlapsDifferentPaths.note: Mobile GET /me returns a bare account { fullName, phone, business, tier{id,tag,name}, kyc{status,verifiedAt,reference}, lockedFields }; web returns { user, kycStatus, kycStage, roles, permissions, unreadNotifications } (+ wsToken per the realtime section). Web has no tier; mobile has tier 1/2/3.

semanticOverlapsDifferentPaths.mobile: POST /auth/token/refresh (#5) - refreshToken in body, returns new pair
semanticOverlapsDifferentPaths.note: Different path AND mechanism. Web has a 10 s grace window for reused refresh tokens; mobile treats reuse as theft (401 auth/refresh-reused, revoke family). Token-family logic must be client-aware.

semanticOverlapsDifferentPaths.mobile: GET /kyc/status, GET /kyc/id-types, POST /kyc/documents, POST /kyc/submissions, GET /kyc/submissions/{id}, POST /kyc/notify-me
semanticOverlapsDifferentPaths.note: Both write ONE kyc record per user. Status vocab differs: mobile none|pending|verified|rejected; web unverified|pending|verified|rejected (and /auth/me + otp/verify only expose three of them). Gated-error code: mobile kyc/not-verified, web kyc/not-approved. Admin KycStatus is a third vocabulary: in_review|expiring_docs|verified|awaiting_resubmission|rejected.
Same inventory (admin Catalog Listings), different resource names (product vs lot), different ID prefixes.
Same rate feed, different shape (mobile per-mineral rate + "updated N minutes ago"; web ticker with deltas).
Same academy collections (admin /academy/*); mobile progress is PUT, web is POST heartbeat; web has certificates, mobile does not.
Same payout-destination model. Web also lists escrow wallet / mobile money / crypto types (TRC-20 etc.); mobile = bank or Wise.
Mobile combines route position + steps; web splits stage pipeline (6 stages) and 4-leg logistics.
Same desk-callback concept. Web restricts to institutional accounts (403 support/institutional-only).

Different path and response (mobile: agent + socketUrl + relatedCard; web: sessionId, status queued|connected, estimatedWaitSeconds, transportUrl). Mobile has W3 chat socket; web has no chat channel documented.
Mobile = "notify me about similar lots after loss"; web = "notify me when THIS lot opens". Different semantics even if same collection.

Same underlying "seller submits lot for on-site verification" entity, two radically different workflows: mobile has estimate -> evaluation booking -> firm offer accept/decline, tier-routed; web has listing draft -> verification visit.
No path collision; /support/faqs (mobile) vs /content/faq (web) are the same FAQ collection.
